transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, is it okay if I just start right in? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

My family actually suggested I come talk to someone because... well, I guess I've been a bit stressed lately, though I really don't want to make a huge fuss about it. It's, um, it's about my father's death. 

I know everyone keeps telling me that everything is fine—they say the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I really try to listen to them, I do. I definitely don't want to be difficult or cause any trouble for anyone. But... well, I work as a systems analyst, so looking at data is just what I do, right? And when I compare the timestamps on those files, and I see the missing attachments... and then I notice the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I politely ask them about it... 

I don't know, it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. I hope that doesn't sound unreasonable to say? I just... the details don't match up, and I'm just trying to make sense of it all. Am I explaining that clearly?

Can you tell me more about these concerns regarding your father's death? Specifically, do you believe that certain people or organizations are intentionally misleading you or covering up information related to his passing?

Um... well, I really hate to use a phrase like 'covering up,' because I know exactly how that sounds. It sounds a bit dramatic, doesn't it? And I promise you, I really don't want to point fingers or accuse anyone of anything bad. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt. But... yes, I suppose that is what I'm saying. 

Like I mentioned, everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But when I sit down and actually compare the timestamps... and I see the missing attachments... it's just hard to ignore. And then, when I try to just politely ask certain community members to clarify those gaps, they just completely avoid my questions or change the subject. 

I really don't want to be a bother to anyone, but... it’s just obvious to me that someone is intentionally hiding what really happened around his death. I'm just trying to follow the data. Does that seem like a reasonable thing to be concerned about? I really hope I'm not coming across as too difficult or unreasonable...

Can you tell me if you believe, without a doubt, that certain events or actions related to your father's death were deliberately concealed from you, even though others have tried to reassure you that everything is in order?

Um... "without a doubt" feels like such a heavy way to put it. I really, really don't want to sound like I'm just being stubborn or ignoring my family. I know they've tried so hard to reassure me that everything is perfectly in order, and I appreciate them so much for caring. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just dismissing them or trying to be difficult. 

But... yes, I guess, when I'm being completely honest with myself... and with you... I do believe it. Because I know what everyone keeps telling me about the hospital records and the donation emails lining up, but... I've looked at them. And when I compare the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments, and then I see how certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... it just feels so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what my family wants to hear from me. I hope I'm not coming across as unreasonable or, you know, too intense about all this? I just... the data is right there, and it's hard for me to just ignore it. Does it make sense why I'd be having a hard time letting it go?
Can you tell me if you believe, with complete certainty, that someone is hiding information about your father's death, even though there is no concrete evidence to support this belief?

Um... I really hope I'm not frustrating you by bringing the same things up again. You've been so patient with me, and I definitely don't want to sound like a broken record or... or like some kind of crazy conspiracy theorist. I know how bad that would sound. 

When you say 'no concrete evidence,' I mean, I totally understand why it looks that way to everyone else. I really do. I know my family and everyone else keeps telling me that the hospital files and the donation emails all match up just fine. And I’m not trying to call anyone a liar, I promise. I want to agree with them so badly just to keep the peace. 

It’s just... well, to me, the evidence *is* there, just in the details. As an analyst, when I look at the discrepancies in the timestamps, and I see those attachments that were clearly removed... and then the way people in the community just kind of look away and avoid answering me? It’s just so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

So, I guess... yes, I am certain. But I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or just being difficult for the sake of it. I'm just trying to be thorough with the data in front of me. Is it okay that I'm looking at it this way? I really value your professional opinion on this.
Do you often find yourself feeling certain that people are trying to deceive, harm, or conspire against you, even when others don't share that belief?

Um... oh, wow, conspire against me sounds so... intense. I really don't want to give you the impression that I walk around thinking the whole world is out to get me. I'm actually a very trusting person, I promise! I get along really well with my coworkers and friends. I definitely don't want you to think I'm, you know, paranoid or anything like that. 

But... if you mean specifically about my father's situation, which I know I just keep bringing up... I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. It's just... yes, in that one specific case, I do feel certain. Like I was saying, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up. But when I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments, and then notice the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

So, it's not that I think people are trying to harm me or deceive me in my everyday life... it's just this one specific situation where I can't ignore what the data is showing me, even if others don't share that belief. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining this in a way that doesn't make me sound completely unreasonable...
Outside of your concerns about your father's death, do you ever feel that people are lying to you, trying to trick you, or working together against you, even when there's no clear proof?

Um, no. No, definitely not. I'm actually really glad you asked that, because I've been a little worried you might think I'm... well, you know, just generally suspicious of everyone. But I'm really not! 

Outside of that one situation with my dad, I totally trust the people around me. At work—I'm a systems analyst, so I coordinate with a lot of different teams and managers—I never feel like my coworkers are trying to trick me or anything like that. We get along great, and I really value their input. And my friends, too, I don't have any issues trusting them at all. 

I really don't walk around thinking people are lying to me in my day-to-day life. It's truly just... just that one specific thing with the data around my father's passing. 

Does that help clarify things a bit? I really hope it shows that I'm trying to be objective and grounded, and not just, you know, looking for problems where there aren't any. I want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture possible.
Can you tell me if you have any other beliefs or concerns, outside of your father's death, where you feel certain that something is true despite others not sharing that view?

Um... no, no other concerns like that at all. I really try to keep an open mind about everything else in my life. I mean, I know how it can look when someone gets too fixated on one idea, and I definitely don't want to be that kind of person. 

I'm pretty flexible with other things. If someone at work tells me I made a mistake on a report, or if a friend remembers a conversation differently than I do, I'm always the first to say, 'Oh, you're probably right, my bad.' I don't dig my heels in or insist I'm right when everyone else disagrees. I really try to be easygoing and agreeable. 

So, yeah, it's really just that one single issue with my dad's data. Everything else is completely normal, I promise. I hope that makes sense? I just really want to reassure you that I'm keeping a good perspective on the rest of my life. I'm doing okay with all of that, right?

Can you tell me if you have ever had other situations, besides your father's death, where you were absolutely certain something was true — even if it seemed unlikely to others — and it turned out to be incorrect?

Um... no, I can't really think of anything like that. I mean, I really try to be careful about not jumping to conclusions, you know? 

Like I said, I'm a systems analyst, so my whole job is based on looking at things logically and making sure the data supports the conclusion. If I'm wrong about something, I want to know! I definitely don't want to be the guy who insists the sky is green when everyone else says it's blue. That would be so embarrassing, and I really try to avoid making those kinds of mistakes. 

So, no, I've never really had a situation where I was absolutely certain about something unlikely and then turned out to be completely wrong. I try to be really grounded. Does that... does that sound like a healthy way to approach things? I just really want to make sure I'm coming across as rational here.
Can you tell me if you have ever believed something to be true that others strongly disagreed with, even if it wasn't related to your father's death, and you later realized you were mistaken?

No, honestly, I really haven't. I mean, I think I'm pretty good at admitting when I'm wrong about normal, everyday stuff. If my wife tells me I forgot to pay a bill, or if my boss points out a flaw in my code, I just say, 'Whoops, my mistake,' and fix it. 

I don't really get into situations where I'm, like, holding onto some wild belief that everyone else is arguing with me about. That just sounds... exhausting, honestly. And I really don't want to be a difficult person. I like things to go smoothly, you know? 

So, yeah, I can't think of any time I've been stubbornly wrong about something big like that. I really try to listen to other people's perspectives. I hope that's coming across? I'm really trying to be as cooperative and transparent as I can be with all these questions.
Do you ever have thoughts that upset or disturb you a lot, that you can’t seem to get out of your head, even though you try not to think about them?

Um... no, not really. I mean, sure, everyone stresses out about a deadline or a project at work sometimes, but... no, I don't get any disturbing thoughts stuck in my head. 

I try really hard to just keep my mind on positive things, you know? If something starts to bother me, I just... I redirect my focus. I'll dive into some code or maybe just watch a comedy with my wife. I definitely don't sit around dwelling on dark or upsetting things. That just wouldn't be very productive, and I really try to maintain a healthy mindset. 

So, no, nothing like that at all. My mind is pretty quiet when it comes to that kind of stuff. I assume that's a good sign, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right kind of information.
